candidates.name: nycdb/nycdb
candidates.what_it_holds: Python ETL that loads 40+ NYC public housing datasets into a Postgres/PostGIS database: PLUTO, HPD violations/complaints/litigations/registrations, DOB job filings/complaints/violations/vacate orders/certificates of occupancy, DOF property sales and tax-lien/J-51/tax-exemption records, ACRIS, Rent Stabilization Unit Counts (annual, by building, back to ~2007), NYCHA developments, executed and marshal evictions, OCA housing-court records, ECB/OATH violations, DHS daily shelter census. Code AGPLv3, database extracts CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, 796+ commits, actively maintained.
candidates.why_useful: Rent Stabilization Unit Counts by building/year is the closest free proxy to 'STR share of housing stock' logic in reverse (regulated long-term supply vs. STR conversion pressure) for NYC, one of our 13 Inside Airbnb panel cities; evictions + HPD violations give a rent-burden/housing-distress proxy at building/tract level to pair with STR registry data (gap #13, also touches #8/#12 municipal registries we already hold for NYC OSE).
candidates.geography: New York City (5 boroughs, building/BBL level, aggregable to tract)
candidates.time_coverage: Varies by dataset; rent stabilization counts ~2007-present, evictions ~2017-present, violations back to 1970s-80s in places
candidates.size_hint: 40+ tables, city-wide, multi-GB when loaded; source CSVs individually much smaller
candidates.license: Code: AGPLv3; data extracts: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
candidates.last_activity: active (796+ commits on main, no exact date surfaced)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Distinct from our NYC OSE STR registry holding; this is long-term-rental/eviction/building-condition data, complementary not duplicate

candidates.name: Housing-Data-Coalition/oca
candidates.what_it_holds: ETL pipeline (Python) that produces 11 deidentified CSV tables from NYS Office of Court Administration NYC Housing Court filings: oca_index, oca_causes (nonpayment vs. holdover etc.), oca_addresses, oca_parties, oca_events, oca_appearances/outcomes, oca_motions, oca_decisions, oca_judgments, oca_warrants (eviction warrants). Covers all NYC landlord-tenant cases, addresses geocoded for tract-level aggregation.
candidates.why_useful: Nonpayment eviction-filing rate by address/tract is a direct, high-frequency rent-burden/housing-distress signal that can be paired with Inside Airbnb NYC listing density to test STR-driven displacement or affordability pressure claims (gap #13/#14 adjacent).
candidates.time_coverage: Not stated precisely in fetched page; OCA records span recent years (court filings ongoing)
candidates.size_hint: 11 CSV tables, city-wide court-filing volume (likely hundreds of thousands of rows across tables)
candidates.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (attribution to OCA, Right to Counsel Coalition, BetaNYC)
candidates.last_activity: not surfaced precisely; org (Housing Data Coalition) appears active with recent repos

candidates.name: walkerke/tidycensus
candidates.what_it_holds: R package/client wrapping the Census Bureau's Decennial Census and ACS 1-/5-year APIs, returning tidyverse data frames with optional tract/block-group/county geometry (sf). Pulls any ACS table including rental vacancy rate (DP04/B25004), gross rent as % of income / rent burden (B25070/B25071), tenure, and housing-unit counts needed to compute an STR-share-of-housing-stock denominator by tract. 768+ commits, actively maintained, requires free Census API key.
candidates.why_useful: This is the standard, well-maintained tool for building the denominator (occupied/vacant housing units, rent burden distribution) that any STR-share-of-housing-stock or rent-burden-vs-STR-density study needs at tract level, nationwide, for any of our 13 Inside Airbnb cities.
candidates.size_hint: N/A - library, not a fixed dataset; pulls arbitrary ACS tables on demand
candidates.last_activity: active, 768 commits, 22 open issues, 4 open PRs at fetch time

candidates.name: xmunoz/sodapy
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client for the Socrata Open Data API (SODA) used by many city/county open-data portals (e.g. NYC, SF, Chicago, LA all run Socrata instances) — supports SoQL queries, pagination, metadata, read/write. 430 stars, 116 forks, 309 commits, MIT license, ownership actively transferred/maintained as of March 2025.
candidates.why_useful: Many of the STR housing-stock, rent-burden, and vacancy datasets we still need (municipal housing-court, rent-registry, or vacancy survey tables) live on Socrata portals per city; this is the general-purpose discovery/pull client called out as a gap-#17 method target rather than a one-off scraper.
candidates.geography: Global (client works against any Socrata-hosted portal)

candidates.name: ckan/ckanapi
candidates.what_it_holds: Official CLI + Python module for the CKAN Action API (CKAN is the open-data portal platform used by many EU cities/national statistics offices and some US agencies). Supports bulk dataset dump/load, remote/local/test targets, parallel workers. 212 stars, 615 commits, MIT/Crown Copyright license, active CI.
candidates.why_useful: Complements sodapy for CKAN-based portals; several EU STR-regulation and housing-registry sources (city/regional open-data catalogues in scope per gap #12/#13) are CKAN-hosted, so this is a working discovery/pull method rather than a bespoke scraper.
candidates.geography: Global (client works against any CKAN-hosted portal)

candidates.name: uscensusbureau/citysdk
candidates.what_it_holds: Official (now archived) Census Bureau JavaScript utility library for Census APIs: statistics pulls plus cartographic GeoJSON and lat/lng-to-FIPS geocoding.
candidates.why_useful: Geocoding utility to map STR listing lat/lng (Inside Airbnb) to census tract/FIPS for joining against ACS vacancy/rent-burden tables; superseded functionally by tidycensus but still a working reference implementation.
candidates.license: not confirmed in fetch (US Census Bureau official repo)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: tidycensus does the statistical-pull half better and is actively maintained; citysdk's only distinct value is the lat/lng->FIPS geocoding helper

candidates.name: tomslee/airbnb-data-collection
candidates.what_it_holds: Tom Slee's original Airbnb listing scraper (Python, Postgres/PostGIS backend) predating Inside Airbnb, used in several 2015-2019 academic STR-housing-impact studies to build historical listing/room-type panels by city. No committed data snapshots or releases in the repo itself; unmaintained since 2019 (Airbnb site-structure changes broke it).
candidates.why_useful: Historically the source many rent-burden/STR-density academic papers used for pre-2015 Inside-Airbnb-era listing counts; flagged only as a method/provenance reference, not for re-running (scrapes airbnb.com directly, which is a terms-of-service decision outside this catalogue's remit per our own repo rules).
candidates.geography: Any city (bounding-box configurable); historically run on many US/EU cities
candidates.size_hint: N/A - scraper only, no committed data
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Superseded by Inside Airbnb which we already hold; this repo itself holds no data, only provenance/method context for older STR-housing papers

I worked around this by WebFetch-ing specific org/repo pages I could name from prior knowledge (NYCDB, Housing Data Coalition, tidycensus, sodapy, ckanapi, Census Bureau, Urban Institute, NYC Planning, GeoDa Center, Eviction Lab, Tom Slee's scraper) rather than running true keyword discovery. This means recall on this theme is materially incomplete — I could not discover repos I didn't already know the name of. Dead ends: Eviction-Lab GitHub org has zero public repos (their eviction/rent-burden-by-tract data is hosted off-GitHub at evictionlab.org, so it's out of scope for this modality but worth a non-GitHub scout flagging); Urban Institute and NYC Planning orgs have hundreds of repos but none of their first ~10 listed (all I could see without working search) were housing/STR-specific; GeoDa Center's visible repos are spatial-analysis software, not housing datasets. Suggest a follow-up pass once the GitHub search rate limit resets (~1hr from 2026-09-14 session time) with the original keyword queries, and also suggest a non-GitHub scout for Eviction Lab, Local Housing Solutions, NLIHC gap data, and HUD USER CHAS/SAFMR downloads directly, since those are real, high-value rent-burden/vacancy sources that simply don't live on GitHub.
